chapter: The Los Angeles music scene in the early 1930s
title: Spencer Johnson, early president of the Black musicians union
summary: Redd supplies that Spencer Johnson preceded Ed Bailey as president of the Black local at 1710 South Central, and Blakeney recalls the name.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Mr. Blakeney, I think before Prez Bailey, there was another person who was the first president of the colored
musicians union as it was called. Incidentally, I know the address there was 1710 South Central Avenue.
That person was from a very prominent family, the Johnson's. There were several school teachers in the family and he was a very outstanding man involved in politics also at the time.
Can you recall his first name?
He was the president before Edward Bailey.
Spencer Johnson; he had a son who was a musician also, Carl. The daughters were schoolteachers; Hilda, Gloria and one other daughter. He was the president prior to Mr. Bailey.
